title: American Express Company FY2022 Form 10-K — Note 20, Income Taxes: unrecognized tax benefits and next-twelve-month sensitivity
key_points: Unrecognized tax benefits were $962 million at December 31, 2022, $1,024 million at December 31, 2021 and $790 million at December 31, 2020.

Of the $962 million at December 31, 2022, approximately $750 million would, if recognized, favorably affect the effective tax rate in a future period (versus $780 million at December 31, 2021 and $580 million at December 31, 2020).

Management states it is reasonably possible that unrecognized tax benefits could decrease within the next twelve months by as much as $150 million, principally from potential resolutions of prior years' tax items with various taxing authorities.
Of that $150 million, approximately $118 million relates to amounts that, if recognized, would impact the effective tax rate in a future period.
Interest and penalties on unrecognized tax benefits were approximately $10 million in FY2022, $40 million in FY2021 and $260 million in FY2020.
Approximately $380 million was accrued for payment of interest and penalties at both December 31, 2022 and December 31, 2021.
FY2022 decreases in unrecognized tax benefits included $74 million of settlements with tax authorities and $104 million of lapses of statute of limitations.
raw_excerpt: Included in the unrecognized tax benefits of $1.0 billion, $1.0 billion and $0.8 billion for December 31, 2022, 2021 and 2020, respectively, are approximately $750 million, $780 million and $580 million, respectively, that, if recognized, would favorably affect the effective tax rate in a future period. We believe it is reasonably possible that our unrecognized tax benefits could decrease within the next twelve months by as much as $150 million, principally as a result of potential resolutions of prior years' tax items with various taxing authorities. ... Of the $150 million of unrecognized tax benefits, approximately $118 million relates to amounts that, if recognized, would impact the effective tax rate in a future period.

title: American Express Company FY2022 Form 10-K — MD&A Business Environment / forward-looking discussion (absence of FY2023 tax-rate guidance)
key_points: The MD&A 'Business Environment' section discusses FY2022 results, capital return and macro uncertainty but states no FY2023 effective tax rate guidance and no normalized tax rate range.

The only quantified forward-looking targets in this section are the CET1 capital ratio target range of 10 to 11 percent and a planned 15 percent increase in the regular quarterly dividend beginning with the first quarter 2023 dividend declaration.
AXP returned $4.9 billion of capital to shareholders during FY2022 through common share repurchases and dividend payments.
The 10-K contains a forward-looking statements cautionary note under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995 covering the MD&A.
The 10-K was filed with the consent of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP dated February 10, 2023, establishing the document date.
raw_excerpt: During the year, we returned $4.9 billion of capital to our shareholders through common share repurchases and dividend payments, while maintaining our Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio within our target range of 10 to 11 percent. ... We also expect to increase the regular quarterly dividend on common shares outstanding by 15 percent beginning with the first quarter 2023 dividend declaration. ... while we recognize the uncertainty of the geopolitical and macroeconomic environment, we remain focused on delivering sustainable and profitable growth.
